question: Can the printed Second Series with January 1832 laboratory reports be treated as an unchanged manuscript dated December 21 1831?

witnesses.claim: The Royal Society lists Second Series manuscript PT/20/5 dated 21 December 1831, read 12 January 1832.
witnesses.limits: Catalog entry (not a byte-verified archival manuscript text); direct web page open cache missed; search indexed metadata verified.

witnesses.claim: Printed Second Series contains Kensington pond, Waterloo Bridge and induced water-current discussions in §§183–190.
witnesses.limits: Original periodical PDF textual opening succeeded, image screenshot cache failed; cannot compare manuscript variant or whether late passages were inserted as note.

witnesses.claim: Editors cite experiment at Kensington Pond on January 10, Waterloo Bridge January 12–13, and 1831 December 28 failed earlier attempt.
witnesses.limits: Dates taken from scholarly editorial annotations referencing original diary, not direct diary witness read.

witnesses.claim: Faraday himself described his Second Series as bearing the date 21 Dec 1831 and read 12 Jan 1832.
witnesses.limits: Retrospective authored letter; accessible search snippet only, full original PDF text and image not independently read this pass.

witnesses.claim: Later volume reproduces Faraday's 1825 entry of no detected induction despite a parallel galvanometer arrangement.
witnesses.limits: Later source quotes notebook; original 1825 notebook handwriting not independently verified.

logical_findings.claim: A copy of 21 Dec 1831 manuscript cannot report experiments performed 12–13 Jan 1832 without subsequent insertion or a chronology discrepancy.
logical_findings.rival: Catalog date may designate first draft; text might have been supplemented during/after delivery, or editorial dated experiment attribution might require correction.

logical_findings.claim: The 21 December 1831 archive manuscript necessarily contains the exact Waterloo Bridge paragraphs of the printed Second Series.
logical_findings.rival: Draft/print variants could be different; 1832 appendices or revised text.

logical_findings.claim: Faraday always adhered to one theory-guided experiment sequence from 1825 to 1832.
logical_findings.rival: 1825 reported failure, 1831 transient detection, December exploratory variations, January negative field tests require multiple practice phases.

next_direct_test.source: Royal Society manuscript PT/20/5 First Series/Second Series + printed 1832 Second Series, §§183–190
next_direct_test.compare: Locate last contemporary entry available in paper dated Dec 21 vs statements requiring Jan 10–13; inspect manuscript marginalia, ink insertions and later corrections.
next_direct_test.no_false_claim: Dated catalog and printed final cannot alone establish when specific paragraphs were added.

originality: historical textual criticism, no new universal MQR law
